Subject: Service Center Staffing Review and Assignment Plan

Context
Our service center operates multiple help desks, counters, and departments that experience steady customer arrivals throughout the day. Each station has a distinct workload profile, and we have several staff types with different skill levels and operating costs. Performance varies by the pairing of staff type and station, reflecting both training and the nature of the service at each location.

Situation
- Customers arrive at each station at a known hourly rate. Some locations consistently see heavier traffic, while others fluctuate.
- Staff handle customers at different speeds depending on both their skill set and the station’s processes. Handling speed is defined as average minutes per customer for each staff type at each station.
- Some staff types are not qualified to serve at certain stations. These restricted combinations cannot be used.
- Each staff type has a finite number of people available for assignment and a distinct hourly cost.

Staffing Challenge
We need to assign available, qualified staff to stations in a way that reliably covers expected arrivals across all locations without overworking team members or leaving gaps in coverage. The combination of many stations and many staff types creates a large number of potential assignments, while qualification limits and differing speeds narrow what is feasible. Balancing speed, coverage, and hourly cost is central to this decision.

Service Quality and Policy Requirements
- Capacity headroom: Handling times are measured in minutes per customer, while arrivals are tracked per hour. Practically, the team placed at each station must, based on their pace at that station, be able to handle more customers in an hour than are expected to arrive. This ensures staff are not working at full stretch continuously and preserves buffer time for variability, short breaks, and administrative tasks. Our utilization policy sets a target fraction of time that staff should be occupied and not exceed.
- Minimum coverage: Each station requires at least a baseline number of staff at all times for safety, front-of-house presence, and uninterrupted service.
- Qualifications: Only trained and approved staff may be assigned to a given station; disallowed pairings must not be used.
- Availability: We cannot assign more employees of a given type than are available for the shift.
- Cost discipline: Each staff type has an hourly cost. While reliability and service quality come first, we aim to cover demand and policies at the lowest feasible total hourly cost.

Goal
Produce a staffing plan that assigns qualified staff types to stations so that:
- Expected demand is met with comfortable headroom in line with the utilization policy.
- Every station meets its minimum coverage requirements.
- No staff type is over-allocated beyond availability.
- Restricted assignments are avoided.
- The total hourly staffing cost is minimized.

Next Steps
We will use the station arrival rates, staff handling times by station, hourly cost rates, headcount availability, utilization target, and minimum coverage levels to evaluate feasible assignments and select a cost-effective plan. The proposed allocation will be reviewed with station leads to ensure practical fit with on-the-ground operations and then trialed with monitoring for adjustments.
